callouts.label: Sleep Changes
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents sleep changes.
callouts.description: Stress can change sleep length, timing, or quality.
callouts.ap_tip: One change alone does not diagnose a condition. Notice patterns that continue or disrupt daily life.

callouts.label: Body Tension
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents body tension.
callouts.description: Headaches, tight muscles, or stomach discomfort can accompany stress.
callouts.ap_tip: Body signals deserve care, not dismissal. A health professional can assess persistent symptoms.

callouts.label: Racing Thoughts
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents racing thoughts.
callouts.description: Worry can make thoughts feel fast, repetitive, or hard to pause.
callouts.ap_tip: Grounding or paced breathing may create a little space. Support is useful when worry feels unmanageable.

callouts.label: Pulling Away
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents pulling away.
callouts.description: Withdrawing from usual people or activities can signal distress.
callouts.ap_tip: Check in with curiosity rather than assumptions. Connection can be gentle and low-pressure.

callouts.label: Concentration Difficulty
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents concentration difficulty.
callouts.description: Stress can make schoolwork and decisions harder.
callouts.ap_tip: Smaller steps and fewer distractions can help. Ask for academic support when needed.

callouts.label: Mood Changes
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents mood changes.
callouts.description: Irritability, sadness, or feeling numb may be stress signals.
callouts.ap_tip: Feelings are information, not character flaws. Sudden or lasting changes merit support.

callouts.label: Restorative Practice
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents restorative practice.
callouts.description: Movement, rest, art, breathing, or time outdoors can support regulation.
callouts.ap_tip: No single practice works for everyone. Choose safe practices that fit the person and culture.

callouts.label: Cultural Healing
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents cultural healing.
callouts.description: Cultural traditions and community practices can strengthen coping and belonging.
callouts.ap_tip: Respect the meaning of a practice to the person. Cultural support can complement professional care.

callouts.label: Peer Listening
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents peer listening.
callouts.description: A peer can listen, validate, and help connect someone to support.
callouts.ap_tip: Peers do not have to solve the problem. Do not promise secrecy when safety may be at risk.

callouts.label: Trusted Adult
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents trusted adult.
callouts.description: A trusted adult can help assess needs and take next steps.
callouts.ap_tip: Keep telling safe adults until someone responds. Examples include family, school, cultural, or community adults.

callouts.label: Professional Support
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents professional support.
callouts.description: Counselors and health professionals can offer assessment and treatment.
callouts.ap_tip: Getting help is a strength. A good fit may take more than one attempt.

callouts.label: Urgent Crisis Help
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents urgent crisis help.
callouts.description: Immediate danger or thoughts of suicide require urgent adult and emergency support.
callouts.ap_tip: Stay with the person when it is safe to do so. Use local emergency or crisis resources; do not manage it alone.
